pairs.question: nullane post manes regis tibi cura perempti, care Dyma, teneant quem iam fortasse uolucres Thebanique canes? patriae quid deinde feretis, Arcades? en reduces contra uenit aspera mater: funus ubi? at nostro semper sub pectore Tydeus saeuit inops tumuli, quamuis patientior artus ille nec abruptis adeo lacrimabilis annis. ire tamen saeuumque libet nullo ordine passim scrutari campum, mediasue inrumpere Thebas.
pairs.derivation: Hopleus's whole speech is an exhortatory appeal built on genuine interrogatives (nullane... cura? quid feretis? funus ubi?) urging Dymas to share his care for the dead king's body. Framing tag 'prior Arcada concitat Hopleus' dropped. The reply (framed by 'excipit orsa Dymas') begins with an oath preamble 'per ego haec uaga sidera iuro, per ducis errantes instar mihi numinis umbras' that does not yet answer; the answer's start is advanced to the operative affirming clause 'idem animus misero' ('my resolve is the same'), which directly answers the appeal. The window ends there (first clean stop); what follows ('comitem circumspicit olim mens... sed nunc prior ibo') is elaboration on going first. pairs.question: quis nouus inceptis rapuit te casus ab armis? quae bello grauiora paras? dic, nate, precanti, cur tibi torua acies? cur hic truculentus in ore pallor, et ad patrios non stant tua lumina uultus? audisti responsa, palam est. per ego oro tuosque, nate, meosque annos miseraeque per ubera matris, ne uati, ne crede, puer! superine profanum dignantur stimulare senem, cui uultus inanis extinctique orbes et poena simillima diro Oedipodae? quid si insidiis et fraude dolosa rex agit, extrema cui nostra in sorte timori nobilitas tuaque ante duces notissima uirtus? illius haec forsan, remur quae uerba deorum; ille monet! ne frena animo permitte calenti, da spatium tenuemque moram, male cuncta ministrat impetus; hoc, oro, munus concede parenti. sic tua maturis signentur tempora canis, et sis ipse parens et ad hunc, animose, timorem peruenias: ne perge meos orbare penates. externi te nempe patres alienaque tangunt pignora? si pudor est, primum miserere tuorum. haec pietas, hic uerus honos; ibi gloria tantum uentosumque decus titulique in morte latentes. nec timidus te flecto parens: i, proelia misce, i Danaas acies mediosque per obuius enses: non teneo; liceat misero tremibunda lauare uulnera et undantem lacrimis siccare cruorem, teque iterum saeuis iterumque remittere bellis. hoc malunt Thebae.
pairs.answer: Sed grauis unanimi casus me fratris ad urbem sponte refert.
pairs.derivation: The father's (Creon's) whole speech opens with genuine interrogatives (quis nouus... casus? quae... paras? cur tibi torua acies?...) asking why his son Menoeceus has abruptly left the fighting and what he plans, then pleads with him not to trust the seer. Framing tag 'tandem pater ante profatus' dropped; the entire speech through 'hoc malunt Thebae' is quoted as the question. The son's reply (framed by 'fraude patrem tacita subit auertitque timorem') opens with a deflecting preamble 'falleris heu uerosque metus, pater optime, nescis. non me ulli monitus, nec uatum exorsa furentum sollicitant... non si ipse... insaniret Apollo' that denies the seer's influence rather than answering why he left; the answer's start is advanced to the operative answering clause 'sed grauis unanimi casus me fratris ad urbem sponte refert', which directly answers 'why did you leave battle.' The window ends at 'refert'; what follows ('gemit Inachia mihi saucius Haemon cuspide...') is elaborating detail on the brother's wound.
